claims: What makes the Jarvis agents work well is 'just a file' -- your exported chat history
Attach a small model (Jev) to tag each conversation with what it got wrong and how you like to use AI; feed the tags back to the main model to generate custom instructions
Most people don't need to build a Jarvis; make the AI you already use work well via custom instructions
On-screen sample: 10 chats classified, got_it_wrong 3, got_it_right 7
how_to_steps: Export all your AI data (ChatGPT Settings > Data controls > Export; Claude equivalent) -> conversations.json
Attach the file to your agent with the prompt: 'This is my whole ChatGPT history. Reverse engineer the custom instructions that turn you into my Jarvis'
Install Jev MCP (uvx jev-mcp-server install claude-code) and run jev_classify over every chat: too verbose? got it wrong? made me repeat?
Bring the classifications back to the main model; it returns a new set of custom instructions
Paste into your custom instructions / CLAUDE.md
on_screen_only: 'Jarvis was a front' title; 'Export all of your AI'
ChatGPT settings nav: Personalization / Profile / Settings (circled) -> Data controls -> Export (circled)

Prompt list: '1. Pull every line I corrected... 2. Keep patterns that show up... 3. Find the version of you that I... 4. Write it as latent space... who it is, who I am to it... 5. Turn each correction into... 6. Paste my own words in as a ve... 7. Add a silent... 8. Under 1,500 characters. A ChatGPT...'

Jev quickstart: '# 1. Get a key: https://console.typesafe.ai/sett... # 2. Install into your client (config is written... uvx jev-mcp-server install claude-code # or: # 3. Diagram: conversations.json -> Jev 'too verbose? yes/no', 'got it wrong? yes/no', 'made me repeat?' -> Claude 'reads only the flagged chats' -> custom instructions
Graph visualisation of chat clusters: Finances, Clients, Sales, Communications

relevance.why: Cheap way to mine years of chat history for a personal preferences file; Haji has already liked this exact idea from the same creator

implement_score.why: One evening: export Claude history, run a classifier (Jev or just Haiku) over chats to flag corrections, have Claude synthesise a <1,500-char preferences block for CLAUDE.md / memory. Jev is optional; a cheap model does the same
